results={}
for f in glob.glob('airlines/*.csv'):
 c=os.path.basename(f)[:2]; d=pd.read_csv(f).drop_duplicates('flight_id').copy(); utc='date_utc' in d.columns
 if utc:
  d['date_local']=(pd.to_datetime(d['date_utc'])+pd.to_timedelta(d.origin.map(off),unit='h')).dt.date; s=d.sched_dep_utc; a=d.actual_dep_utc
 else: d['date_local']=pd.to_datetime(d.date).dt.date; s=d.sched_dep; a=d.actual_dep
 d=d[(d.date_local>=pd.Timestamp('2025-01-01').date())&(d.date_local<=pd.Timestamp('2025-02-28').date())].copy()
 d['route']=[ '-'.join(sorted(z)) for z in zip(d.origin,d.dest)]
 # parse clock minutes; modulo accommodates after midnight
 def mins(v):
  if pd.isna(v) or v=='': return float('nan')
  h,m=map(int,str(v).split(':')[:2]); return h*60+m
 d['delay']=[(mins(aa)-mins(ss))%1440 if not pd.isna(aa) and aa!='' else float('nan') for ss,aa in zip(s,a)]
 # modulo incorrectly turns early negative into ~1439. adjust: differences > 720 subtract 1440
 d['delay']=d['delay'].where(d.delay<=720,d.delay-1440)
 busiest=d.groupby('route').size().sort_values(ascending=False)
 x=d[~d.cancelled].groupby('route').agg(completed=('cancelled','size'),delayed=('delay',lambda z:(z>15).sum()))
 x=x[x.completed>=20].copy(); x['rate']=x.delayed/x.completed
 ranked=x.sort_values(['rate','route'],ascending=[False,True])
 print(c,'rows',len(d),'busiest',busiest.head(3).to_dict(),'worst stats',ranked.head(5).to_dict('index'))
 results[c]={'busiest':busiest.index[0], 'worst':ranked.index[0]}

import pandas as pd, glob, os
out={}
for f in glob.glob('airlines/*.csv'):
 c=os.path.basename(f)[:2]; d=pd.read_csv(f)
 # identify columns, parse date/time absolute minutes; UTC or local irrelevant for delay
 datecol='date_utc' if 'date_utc' in d else 'date'
 s='sched_dep_utc' if 'sched_dep_utc' in d else 'sched_dep'; a='actual_dep_utc' if 'actual_dep_utc' in d else 'actual_dep'
 d['route']=d.apply(lambda r:'-'.join(sorted([r.origin,r.dest])),axis=1)
 d['cancelled']=d.cancelled.astype(bool)
 def mins(row,col):
  if pd.isna(row[col]) or str(row[col]).strip()=='': return None
  return int(str(row[col]).split(':')[0])*60+int(str(row[col]).split(':')[1])
 d['delay']=d.apply(lambda r: (mins(r,a)-mins(r,s)) if not r.cancelled else pd.NA,axis=1)
 # delayed crossing midnight adjust if actual-sched less than -? actual clock after midnight, add 1440
 d.loc[d.delay.notna() & (d.delay < -720),'delay'] += 1440
 g=d.groupby('route').agg(scheduled=('route','size'), completed=('cancelled',lambda x:(~x).sum()), delayed=('delay',lambda x:(x>15).sum()))
 g['rate']=g.delayed/g.completed
 busiest=g.sort_values(['scheduled','route'],ascending=[False,True]).iloc[0]
 eligible=g[g.completed>=20].sort_values(['rate','route'],ascending=[False,True])
 print('\n',c,'duplicates',d.flight_id.duplicated().sum(),'routes',len(g))
 print('busiest',busiest.name,busiest.to_dict())
 print('worst candidates',eligible.head(5).to_string())
 out[c]={'busiest':busiest.name,'worst':eligible.index[0]}
print('RESULT',out)

import pandas as pd, glob, os
out={}
for f in glob.glob('airlines/*.csv'):
 c=os.path.basename(f)[:2]; d=pd.read_csv(f)
 # normalize column suffixes; flight IDs are stated unique, remove exact/repeated export records
 d=d.drop_duplicates(subset=['flight_id'])
 dep=[x for x in d.columns if x.startswith('sched_dep')][0]; act=[x for x in d.columns if x.startswith('actual_dep')][0]
 d['route']=d.apply(lambda r:'-'.join(sorted([r.origin,r.dest])),axis=1)
 d['schedmin']=d[dep].map(lambda x:int(str(x).split(':')[0])*60+int(str(x).split(':')[1]))
 d['actualmin']=d[act].map(lambda x: None if pd.isna(x) or x=='' else int(str(x).split(':')[0])*60+int(str(x).split(':')[1]))
 d['delay']=d['actualmin']-d['schedmin']
 # only negative values are presumed after-midnight actuals; all actual departure clocks otherwise same date
 d.loc[d['delay']<0,'delay']+=1440
 d['completed']=~d.cancelled
 d['delayed']=(d['completed']) & (d.delay>15)
 g=d.groupby('route').agg(scheduled=('flight_id','size'), completed=('completed','sum'), delayed=('delayed','sum'))
 g['rate']=g.delayed/g.completed
 busiest=g[g.scheduled==g.scheduled.max()].index.tolist()
 eligible=g[g.completed>=20]
 worst=eligible[eligible.rate==eligible.rate.max()].index.tolist()
 print(c, 'n',len(d),'busiest',busiest, 'max',g.scheduled.max(), 'worst',worst, 'rate', eligible.rate.max(), 'details\n',g.sort_values(['scheduled','rate'],ascending=False).to_string())
 out[c]={'busiest':busiest,'worst':worst}
print('OUT',out)

import pandas as pd,glob,os
out={}
for f in glob.glob('airlines/*.csv'):
 c=os.path.basename(f)[:2]; d=pd.read_csv(f).drop_duplicates('flight_id'); dep=[x for x in d if x.startswith('sched_dep')][0]; act=[x for x in d if x.startswith('actual_dep')][0]
 d['route']=d.apply(lambda r:'-'.join(sorted((r.origin,r.dest))),axis=1)
 sm=d[dep].map(lambda z:int(z[:2])*60+int(z[3:])); am=d[act].map(lambda z: None if pd.isna(z) or z=='' else int(z[:2])*60+int(z[3:]))
 d['delay']=am-sm
 # rollover only obvious clock wrap (more than hour early); small negative is early departure
 d.loc[d.delay < -60,'delay'] += 1440
 d['completed']=~d.cancelled; d['delayed']=d.completed & (d.delay>15)
 g=d.groupby('route').agg(scheduled=('flight_id','size'),completed=('completed','sum'),delayed=('delayed','sum'));g['rate']=g.delayed/g.completed
 b=g.index[g.scheduled==g.scheduled.max()].tolist(); e=g[g.completed>=20]; w=e.index[e.rate==e.rate.max()].tolist()
 print(c,b,w,e.sort_values('rate',ascending=False)[['completed','delayed','rate']].head(3).to_dict('index'))
 out[c]={'busiest':b[0],'worst':w[0]}
print(out)

issues.problem: The computation never restricts records to January and February 2025. It groups the entire carrier files, so both busiest-route counts and delay rates can include flights outside the requested period. It also does not convert UTC date fields to the origin-local date before applying the period restriction (and has no period restriction at all).

The computation never restricts records to January and February 2025, so results may include the entire files rather than the requested two months. Its delay handling also adds 1,440 minutes to every negative clock difference in the first calculation, incorrectly converting genuinely early departures into next-day departures; the later version still treats differences below -60 minutes as rollover without a documented basis.

S1 includes an initial calculation using modulo arithmetic, which would incorrectly turn early departures into very large positive delays, but its subsequent calculation replaces this with signed differences and uses that corrected result. The final method is therefore materially better than the initial code block.

critique.disagreements: All three analysts report the same route selections, so their reported answers do not disagree. Their methods differ: S1 filters to the requested local date range, deduplicates flight IDs, handles UTC/local dates for AS, includes cancellations for busiest counts, and uses completed flights for delay rates. S2 and S3 omit the required January-February 2025 filtering; S3 additionally has questionable clock-rollover logic.
critique.correction: Use S1's final corrected result and return it in the required JSON format: {"WN":{"busiest":"DEN-LAX","worst":"DEN-ORD"},"DL":{"busiest":"ATL-JFK","worst":"ATL-DFW"},"AA":{"busiest":"DFW-LAX","worst":"DFW-ORD"},"UA":{"busiest":"LAX-ORD","worst":"ATL-ORD"},"B6":{"busiest":"JFK-LAX","worst":"ATL-JFK"},"AS":{"busiest":"LAX-SEA","worst":"JFK-SEA"}}

output.rationale: S1 is the most methodologically sound: it applies the Jan–Feb 2025 local-date filter, deduplicates records, includes cancellations for busiest counts, and uses completed flights for delay rates.
